teaser.text: Brookfield Corporation (BN) owns businesses that customers pay to use and an investment manager that investors pay to manage their money. To understand how a dollar moves through Brookfield, follow it from the customer or investor to the business, then through costs, lenders and outside owners before asking what remains for BN.

blocks.heading: Where could Brookfield’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s central outcome is a gradual rerating supported by rising NAV per share. The weighted price is 65.47 in October 2027, including dividends, for a 24% return from today’s 52.95. It reaches 78.16 in October 2028, equal to a 49% return. By October 2029, the weighted price is 92.17, equal to a 77% return.

The 2029 range is 44.28 to 144.13. Today’s price is 52.95. The probabilities are 25% for bear, 55% for base and 20% for bull, reflecting stronger evidence for moderate growth than for either a severe setback or a near-complete discount closure.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Brookfield?

paragraphs.text: Faster deployment, profitable insurance growth and realized carry would support the base or bull case. Delayed exits, refinancing pressure or weaker private marks would move the outlook toward bear. Brookfield’s Q3 2026 results call is scheduled for November 12, 2026. The company expects to move to U.S. GAAP from January 1, 2027. The investment case rests on turning committed capital, insurance growth and unrealized value into durable per-share earnings and cash.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Brookfield really make?

paragraphs.subsection: 6.5 — What the price implies — the sum of the parts
paragraphs.text: Finally, the parent consumes cash. Corporate operating FFO was negative US$530 million over the twelve months ended June 2026, including US$747 million of corporate borrowing interest. Brookfield must show that reinvestment, acquisitions and buybacks increase realizable cash earnings per share after those claims.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Brookfield today?

paragraphs.text: The usual P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, needs care here. Accounting profit can fall when an office building’s estimated value declines even though tenants keep paying rent. It can also rise when Brookfield sells an investment for a gain that will not recur. Distributable earnings, or DE, is intended to show earnings more closely connected to usable cash. DE before realizations was US$2.39 per share for the twelve months ended June 2026, while realized carried interest added US$520 million. A low P/E is less persuasive when its denominator contains unusual sale profits.

blocks.heading: Is Brookfield's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Brookfield has generally kept most of its recurring parent-level earnings for growth, while using buybacks to increase each remaining shareholder’s ownership. Its “distributable earnings before realizations” is a management-defined measure of recurring earnings available for dividends or reinvestment. It excludes realized investment-sale gains and realized performance fees, so it is not simply cash sitting in a bank account.

Buybacks are another use of capital. They can raise each remaining share’s claim on the business, but they do not by themselves prove that the businesses improved. Comparable earnings before realizations per share rose from US$1.22 in 2021 to US$2.27 in 2025. The result is encouraging, though the separate effects of acquisitions, operating improvement, financing and repurchases are not fully visible.

paragraphs.text: Base dividends are $0.30 in 2027 and $0.32 in 2028. They reach $0.34 in 2029. The bear holds the annualized payout at $0.28, while the bull reaches $0.31, $0.34 and $0.36. The base follows management’s 7% growth assumption and the record of regular increases from 2023 through 2025.

The forecast would move toward the bear case if 2027–2029 exits are delayed or priced below carrying values. That would restrain realized carry, net income and EPS, while weak property values and refinancing costs would pressure operating earnings and the multiple.

blocks.heading: What has Brookfield guided for earnings and returns?

paragraphs.text: On September 17, 2026, Brookfield presented an illustrative five-year plan with a plan value of $140 per share in 2031. Plan value is management’s estimate of what its businesses and investments might be worth if its assumptions work. It is like valuing a house after planned renovations: the result depends on future profits, sale prices and what buyers will pay. It is not cash, reported book value or a promise that the market will pay that price.

blocks.heading: Has Brookfield kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Brookfield also has a measurable promise to assess. At its September 2026 investor day, it compared a US$5.6 billion target for distributable earnings before realizations with US$5.7 billion achieved for the 2021–2026 comparison. This measure excludes certain investment realizations, so it tests recurring earnings more directly. Distributable earnings per share rose from US$1.29 to US$2.54 over the comparison period.

blocks.heading: What is Brookfield's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Revenue and operating earnings both increased, with operating earnings growing faster. Shareholder net income and diluted EPS also rose, but the result included acquisitions, changes in ownership and unusual items. Just Group, a British retirement insurer, contributed its first full quarter after Brookfield acquired it, helping Wealth Solutions DE reach US$480 million.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Brookfield's next results?

paragraphs.text: Brookfield has scheduled its Q3 2026 call for November 12, 2026. The first test is whether fundraising becomes fee-producing deployment and whether mature investments return cash. Brookfield Asset Management reported $68 billion of uncalled commitments that would generate approximately $680 million of annual fees once deployed. The condition matters: commitments prepare future earnings, but delayed deployment delays fees and later exits.
